title: Soup Sieve descendant selectors can exhaust CPU on deeply nested markup
summary: Small, deeply nested HTML or XML can make ordinary descendant selectors consume excessive CPU, including through Beautiful Soup. Soup Sieve 4.0 fixes the matching algorithm with default caching.

severity.rationale: Untrusted fetched markup can stall scrapers and agent retrieval workers without attacker control of the selector. The documented impact is denial of service, warranting a 30-day response.

affected.note: Versions before 4.0 are affected. NOCACHE retains vulnerable matching even after upgrading.

exposure: Applications selecting only trusted documents are outside this exposure. Scrapers processing untrusted markup with descendant combinators are exposed.

params.instructions: Check whether selectors use NOCACHE with descendant combinators on untrusted documents, even on version 4.0 or later.

remediation.action: Update or contain the affected component
remediation.details: Upgrade to 4.0 or later and retain default caching. Avoid NOCACHE for untrusted input. Before upgrading, limit document depth and selection time.
remediation.risk: Low. Test selector results after the caching change.

verification: Confirm the runtime version and that untrusted-input selection uses caching.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
